subject.title: Manage Claw cron jobs through the gateway

question: Should scheduler cleanup for Claw-created agents remain solely in the experimental Claw lifecycle, or should ordinary `agents delete` become the canonical cleanup owner for these agent-scoped Gateway jobs?
rationale: Both choices affect durable ownership, operator expectations, and whether a normal agent deletion can leave experimental scheduler work behind; the repository policy requires maintainer intent for that cross-boundary lifecycle contract.

options.title: Keep cleanup Claw-owned
options.body: Keep the feature scoped to Claw provenance and separately track any generic agent-delete scheduler cleanup after the experimental contract stabilizes.

options.title: Extend normal agent deletion
options.body: Make `agents delete` remove verified agent-owned scheduler jobs so deleting a Claw agent through the normal CLI cannot leave recurring work behind.

recommendation.title: Keep cleanup Claw-owned
recommendation.body: Keep the feature scoped to Claw provenance and separately track any generic agent-delete scheduler cleanup after the experimental contract stabilizes.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review established the competing deletion-boundary requirements and they are assigned to the PR.
